title: Alibaba prepares Qwen Go personal AI assistant for claims, bookings and shopping
source_used: TechNode (read in full; short), which cites National Business Daily in Chinese
key_facts: Alibaba is preparing to introduce Qwen Go, a personal AI assistant for tasks such as flight-delay compensation claims, shopping refunds, car-servicing appointments and sports-venue bookings (TechNode).
Reports on 13 Oct 2026 described trials in which the assistant accessed services, compared options and contacted customer support on users' behalf.

In one shared demonstration Qwen Go checked a user's flight history, identified an eligible delay and negotiated RMB 70 in cash compensation after a phone call failed and it switched to text-based customer support.
Its actions were visible on screen and the user could intervene or stop the process.
The upgrade builds on Qwen's existing connections to Alibaba services for shopping, transport and deliveries.
The underlying report is credited to National Business Daily (in Chinese); no Alibaba statement is quoted.
quote_evidence: Alibaba is preparing to introduce Qwen Go, a personal AI assistant that can handle tasks such as flight-delay compensation claims, shopping refunds, car-servicing appointments and sports-venue bookings.
Its actions were visible on screen, and the user could intervene or stop the process.

why_it_matters_hint: A large Chinese e-commerce group is testing an assistant that handles claims and bookings for users, with a person able to stop it.
notes: Short article. The original report is National Business Daily (Chinese), not read; TechNode relays it. No launch date or Alibaba statement.
